purpose: Curated cross_lingual and role_query specs for `python3 -m living_memory.retrieval_harness build-goldset --seed-queries`. Committed so artifacts/harness/goldset.jsonl regenerates byte-identically from the frozen snapshot.

snapshot.source_db: ~/.local/share/living-memory/global.sqlite3 (opened file:...?mode=ro, copied with the sqlite backup API)

cross_lingual_rule: Russian jargon query vs its plain-English paraphrase, both run through the real MemoryRecallService on the snapshot with the same scope/depth. relevant_node_ids are resolved MECHANICALLY as the paraphrase query's top_k results (top_k=1: the single node the plain-language question surfaces first) — never hand-picked. A pair was kept only if, measured on the snapshot: (a) the paraphrase's top-1 vector similarity >= 0.40, (b) that node's content is predominantly Latin-script (English), (c) the jargon query scores STRICTLY LOWER on the same node (cosine) and does not already rank it first, and (d) the node is topically about the query's subject. 60+ authored pairs were measured; the ones where the jargon query already won (e.g. 'тесты флакуют' 0.5054 > 0.3484, 'дубликаты узлов схлопываются' 0.4805 > 0.3624, 'ядра пластичного обновления' 0.6331 > 0.5856) were dropped, because they prove nothing about the gap. Every kept item records both scores in provenance (paraphrase_top_k[].vector_score vs jargon_vector_scores).
role_query_rule: Role/procedural queries whose answer is an active level:schema procedure carrying context.trigger; the builder re-validates active + level='schema' + context.trigger for every expected id and records the trigger as justification. Node ids were mined from the snapshot's 433 active schema nodes; where a procedure exists as several identical copies, ALL copies are named so retrieval is not penalised for returning a twin. scope is the procedure's own scope, so the item measures ranking rather than the scope gate. Roughly two thirds of the queries are phrased from material that lives BEYOND the 128-token visible span of the node (tail queries); the tail flag itself is computed by the harness.

measured_build.note: Numbers below were measured on the frozen snapshot at freeze time; `--build-report` reproduces them. This block is documentation only — the builder reads just `cross_lingual` and `role_query`, so it cannot influence the goldset.

content_grounded_selection.sampling: random.Random(20260817).sample over the sorted eligible event ids, then re-sorted
content_grounded_selection.relevant_nodes_per_item: 1..15 (median 3); the containment label keeps every result of the event whose IDF containment against the consuming trace is >= 0.12
content_grounded_selection.scope_skew: project:x 110, project:online 26, project:ae 12, project:lm 6, global 2, other 4 — the natural distribution of labelled events after the cutoff, not a design choice

cross_lingual_scores.measured_on: 38 kept pairs, one relevant node each
cross_lingual_scores.reference: the failure class measured 2026-08-17 on the live DB: поревьювь / мердж-реквест / апрув score cos 0.201-0.392 where ordinary lexicon scores 0.75-0.83

tail.rule: an item is tail iff every relevant node with a non-empty grounding-token set has all occurrences of all those tokens at char offset >= visible_char_end, where visible_char_end comes from the real paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 tokenizer at max_seq_length=128 (specials dropped). Full text is in TAIL_RULE and is copied into every item's provenance.tail_classification.rule.
tail.why_content_grounded_is_never_tail: the containment label selects results sharing a lot of vocabulary with the consuming trace, so at least one grounding token always lands inside the visible prefix — 0 of 160 sampled items are tail. The tail subset therefore comes from the curated role_query specs, whose queries were written from material past the node's visible span and verified with the harness classifier.
